title: Americans in Gaza: Financiers of a Graveyard
author: M. Reza Behnam
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/09/Damage_in_Gaza_Strip_during_the_October_2023_-_29-680x479.jpg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/11/americans-
in-gaza-financiers-of-a-graveyard-2/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2024/09/Damage_in_Gaza_Strip_during_the_October_2023_-_29-680x479.jpg)

Photograph Source: WAFA (Q2915969) - [CC BY-SA
3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)

The protracted slaughter in Gaza stands as one of the defining moral
catastrophes of the modern era. With tens of thousands of Palestinians killed,
disproportionately women, children and infants, the descent of an entire
enclave into manufactured famine, medical collapse and total annihilation has
unfolded in real time.

This is not happening in the dark. It is happening in broad daylight; funded,
diplomatically shielded and witnessed by the world. To examine the shameful
silence of the American public and motivations of the Zionist state after
nearly three years of this horror, is to confront a profound erosion of
collective humanity.

For citizens of the United States, this genocide has exposed a dark reality:
personal ease and comfort have been prioritized over conscience.

The bombs flattening apartment blocks, tent camps and the entirety of Gaza,
are branded with “Made in the USA” and paid for with billions of dollars
plucked from American taxpayers. The diversion of public funds towards the
slaughter in Gaza, while domestic pillars like healthcare, housing and
education deteriorate, renders our silence a form of complicity. We have
become the financiers of a graveyard.

For millions, the genocide is a skip through disposable news notifications.
The silence of the American majority reveals moral insulation—a dangerous
belief that oceans can guarantee sanctuary from the consequences of our
government’s imperial and murderous foreign policy.

Many who claim to oppose the violence retreat into a paralyzing apathy,
convincing themselves that the institutional machinery is too big and complex
to control. History, however, will not record this as powerlessness; it will
be remembered as acquiescence. When faced with the industrial-scale erasure of
a population, silence is not neutral; it is a disposition that allows the
machine to keep grinding on.

The genocidal war on Gaza has also unmasked the [internal ethical rot
](https://www.972mag.com/dehumanization-moral-abyss-israelis/)and
normalization of violence with Israeli society. That this level of devastation
has been sustained with broad domestic backing for so long, reveals a deep
societal crisis. Decades of militarism, occupation and state-sanctioned
apartheid have fostered an environment in which civilian deaths are
celebrated, justified or callously ignored by the Israeli public.

The military assault that began following the 7 October 2023, Palestinian
prison break, mutated long ago into a sustained campaign of dehumanization and
societal eradication. The methodical targeting of journalists, poets, health
care providers, teachers and bakers proves that retaliation was not the
objective; that the real goal has been to wipe out generations of Palestinian
families, to make recovery impossible and the land uninhabitable.

Shielded by United Nations vetoes and unconstrained American patronage, the
Israeli regime has operated under the dangerous assumption that it is entirely
immune from international law and sanctions. This absolute impunity has not
made Israeli society safer; instead, it has underscored that a state without a
moral compass, that breaks all the rules, will eventually fail.

The illusion of a “rules-based” international legal order has been shattered
after three years of unrestrained genocide. The silence of the American
witness and the brutality of the Israeli perpetrator are of an inseparable
piece—one driven by comfortable detachment and the other by supremacist
violence.

When the dust finally settles over the rubble of Gaza, judgment and indictment
will not be only against those who pulled the trigger and dropped the
payloads, but against those who knew and said nothing.
